answers.label: Benefits and challenges of consequential methods
answers.text:
Challenges:
• Lifetime quantification of impacts is subject to uncertainties and errors similar to those seen historically in carbon offset REDD+ projects, which can change significantly from what may have seemed reasonable or logical in the original year the estimations were made.
• Setting boundaries as system-wide can introduce further uncertainties on the impact of such projects, which can be variable across large and complex electrical grid systems, and thus harder to quantify accurately. They also make the value proposition for any organization less clear, as they may not get the anticipated credit for bringing online new renewable electricity due to factors outside of their control (and often, visibility). Organizations may be less inclined to make such investments as a result.
Feasibility:
• Substantially more data and information would need to be readily available publicly to properly assess the system-wide potential impacts of project considerations than exist today.
• As the impacts being considered for Consequential Accounting are typically outside of organizations core objectives, including SBTi organizational targets, additional administrative burden to quantify and report such consequential accounting requirements disincentivizes organizations from participating in such projects, accounting, and reporting.

answers.label: Appropriateness of the TWG subgroup formula
Why the formula is or is not appropriate
answers.text: Quantification of a marginal emission rate applicable to grid region on an annual basis is reasonable. Requiring an hourly accounting of such emission rates is not, and represents a significant unnecessary burden to reasonably quantify the impact of such projects. The difference between them is a ~1,350-fold increase in data points from 12 monthly bills and 1 annual emission factor to 8,760 hourly usage amounts and an equal amount of emission factors, per geography. The marginal benefit for such an accounting undertaking is unclear.

answers.label: Secondary effects to consider, and how
Why secondary effects should be excluded
answers.text: It should not be the responsibility of organizations to consider how the grid might respond to a renewable project implemented for the benefit of said organization. The organization is seeking to reduce its own footprint by controlling what it can control. It is the responsibility of grid operators, utilities, and governments to manage electricity grid systems properly, accounting for the market forces as they change over time.

answers.label: Annual versus lifetime impact reporting
selections: Reported once for the lifetime of the project

answers.label: Why annual or lifetime reporting
answers.text: Similar to the current Scope 3.11 methodology for sold goods and services total lifetime footprinting, a reasonable estimate for the lifetime of the project should be made at the initial project completion. There is no additional value-add from quantifying projects each year, and no additional decarbonization actions that will result from such an accounting exercise.

answers.label: Requiredness of the financial analysis test
Requiredness of the common practice test
Why selected tests should be included
answers.text:
• Timing: To claim additionality, an organization’s actions should contribute towards the additional generation brought online in a demonstrable way. Purchases of existing/legacy generation projects are challenged to claim they added to RE build-out.
• Positive List: Providing a list of preferred project types is helpful when organizations are considering RE procurement options. This list should be maintained and updated regularly.

answers.label: Context on test feasibility
answers.text:
• Financial Analysis: Difficult to determine if the project would or would not have been pursued without the additional revenue stream, as there are many variables for “go/no go” decisions.
• Barrier: How to demonstrate if significant technological, institutional, or market barriers exist which would have prevented the project from moving forward, and that the incentive overcame these barriers?
• Common Practice: How to determine what is “common practice” in any region, especially as rapid shifts can occur between what is done today and what is done in just a few years (e.g. large policy shifts with a governing regime change)?

answers.label: Additionality tests missing from the framework
Regions warranting different tests, with examples
Details on operating margin methodologies
answers.text:
• SCED – locational: inappropriate to estimate marginal emissions rates for each node of the grid
• Heat-rate/LMP: inappropriate to assume LMP reflects the variable operating cost of the marginal unit, then using it to infer the heat rate of the marginal unit and combining with assumptions about the fuel by of the marginal unit.

answers.label: Details on build margin methodologies
answers.text:
• Policy Scenario: RE deployment has not shown to historically match well with stated policies and thus may paint an inaccurate picture of what will realistically be built in the future.
• Capacity expansion modelling: Uses scenarios based on estimated future buildout, which is subject to error.

answers.label: Assessing model applicability to project types
answers.text: Recommend not to use future-looking models, but instead use historical and current actual data, based on deviations between prior predictions and actual results seen.

answers.label: Other appropriate emission rates or metrics
Why that spatial granularity ceiling
answers.text: Countries can widely vary in size – those that are smaller can comfortably utilize a country-level granularity for marginal emission rates. Some countries may have grid region data readily available, which may be used for such calculations. Because this question asks what the maximum appropriate level is, country is appropriate.

answers.label: Why that temporal granularity ceiling
answers.text: Matching our view of Scope 2 accounting best practices, annual accounting and RE procurement is sufficient to accelerate decarbonization and quantify its impacts.

answers.label: Appropriate margin weighting approaches
selections: GHG Protocol Guidelines for Quantifying GHG Reductions from Grid-connected Electricity Projects

answers.label: Why selected weighting approaches are appropriate
answers.text: GHG Protocol and UNFCCC approaches provide methodologies to assess impacts based on multiple project factors and generate a reasonable build & operating margin weighting.
